C0.quote: the maximum payment rule (MP). Under this rule, each voter controls a part of the budget
C0.note: Approval-based budget division rules aggregating approval ballots into a distribution; treated as a voting procedure.

C1.quote: MP meets our criteria as it satisfies monotonicity and a demanding population consistency condition
C1.note: Mostly axiomatic (monotonicity, population consistency, approximate fairness AFS/core satisfaction). Approximation ratios to fairness axioms are quantitative axiomatic analysis; WD included for the efficiency/approximation aspects, weakly. The strategyproofness remark is minor.

C2.1.quote: each voter i ∈ N reports his preferences in the form of an approval ballot

C2.2.quote: We assume that the voters have dichotomous preferences over the candidates
C2.2.note: Input is approval sets; the paper also describes preferences as dichotomous.

C2.3.quote: voters only distinguish between approved and disapproved candidates
C2.3.note: Dichotomous preferences and utilities ui(p) are attributed to voters.

C2.4.quote: we assume that the utility of a voter i for a distribution p is
C2.4.note: Ballot is described as how a voter reports his preferences, and the rule is applied directly; no statement that reports equal preferences or may differ. Remark 4 discusses manipulation briefly but no model separation.

C3.1.quote: While MP is monotonic, it fails the more demanding property of strategyproofness.
C3.1.note: Only a single example of manipulability; no main analysis considers strategic voters.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held attitude.

C4.1.quote: the utility of a voter i for a distribution p is the total share
C4.1.note: Utility is defined as total share assigned to approved candidates.

C4.2.quote: ui ( p) = ∑ x∈ Ai p( x )
C4.2.note: Utility is the total share of approved candidates (utility 1 per unit share for approved, 0 otherwise), stated in the model.

C5.1.note: AFS and core are proportionality/representation fairness notions to groups of voters; also efficiency discussed in Remark 2.

C5.2.quote: Average fair share (AFS) lower bounds the average utility of every group of voters
C5.2.note: Utilities are defined from the approval ballots; no statement relating ballots to held attitudes.

VOT.quote_behav: each voter i ∈ N reports his preferences in the form of an approval ballot
VOT.note: Voters submit ballots, fixed by the model; the manipulation example in Remark 4 is not a main analysis.

C8.1.note: NA: no type is STRAT or MIXED.

claims.quote: these properties make a strong case for using MP in practice.
MP is the only sequential payment rule that satisfies our original desiderata
in practice, we believe that it is rare for MP to return (severely) inefficient outcomes

C9.1.note: Claims about which rule to use and practical performance.

C9.2.note: Claims about fairness to voters and use in practice need an assumption that ballots reflect voters' held preferences (sincere reporting) and that utilities are approval-based; sincerity is not stated, while the utility link is stated.

C10.1.note: No statement of purely procedural reading.
